name: Spare Research
replaces: Journal paywalls and the fees researchers pay to publish openly
summary: Research that is free to read and free to publish, with open peer review and permanent links for citing. Papers are posted, screened, reviewed in the open and gathered into journals that editors run on top. It hosts only papers the authors have the right to share, keeps every version, and shows corrections and retractions openly. People, scripts and AI agents all use the same commands.

areas.name: Getting started: accounts, researcher profiles and ORCID
areas.summary: One Spareware login, a researcher profile linked to ORCID and ROR, reading with no account at all, and the first steps for readers, authors, reviewers and editors.

features.name: Sign up and sign in
features.does: Create one Spareware login and use it to submit, review and edit on any device.

parts.name: Kit sign-in in Spare Research
parts.what: Uses the kit's sign-up, passkeys and sign-in screens, and asks for the second sign-in step from editors, screeners and moderators.

parts.name: Research roles
parts.what: Reader, author, reviewer, editor, screener and moderator roles on the kit's roles per app, each with its own checks.

features.name: Read without an account
features.does: Read, download, search and cite any paper with no account, no sign-in wall and no tracking.

parts.name: Open reading with no account
parts.what: Every paper page, file and published review is public and served without tracking cookies or a sign-in; an account is needed only to submit, review, follow or comment.

parts.name: Reading settings without an account
parts.what: Keeps reading settings and a saved list on the device with no account, and moves them in if the reader signs up later.

features.name: Link my ORCID iD
features.does: Prove my ORCID iD once, so my papers and reviews are credited to me everywhere.

parts.name: ORCID sign-in link
parts.what: Proves a person holds an ORCID iD through ORCID's own sign-in (OAuth), so nobody can claim someone else's iD by typing it in.

parts.name: ORCID terms and membership
parts.what: ORCID's free public API is for non-commercial use with daily read limits; adding works and reviews to records needs the member API, about USD 4,775 a year for a non-profit in 2026. Which fits a co-op running at cost.

parts.name: ORCID record sync
parts.what: With the person's permission, adds their papers and reviews to their ORCID record, and reads their affiliations and past works in.

features.name: Researcher profile
features.does: Show my name, affiliations, fields, papers and reviews on one public page.

parts.name: Researcher profile model
parts.what: Adds name variants, the ORCID iD, affiliations with dates, fields and languages to the kit's profile, with who can see each set by the person.

parts.name: Profile page
parts.what: A public page with the person's papers, the reviews they chose to sign, the journals they edit and a way to contact them through the app.

features.name: Affiliations from an open list
features.does: Pick my university or institute from an open list, so my affiliation is written the same way everywhere.

parts.name: ROR registry data
parts.what: Loads the open Research Organization Registry (ROR, CC0 data) and keeps it current, with names in several languages.

parts.name: Affiliation picker
parts.what: Type-ahead search over ROR, with past affiliations kept by date and a free-text option for places not yet listed, offered to ROR as a suggestion.

features.name: Change my name with care
features.does: Change my name on every paper and review I wrote, without the old name staying on show.

parts.name: Name change across the record
parts.what: Updates the author name on every version, review and metadata record, sends corrected metadata to the DOI agency, and leaves no public trace of the old name unless the person asks.

features.name: First steps for each role
features.does: Get a short guide the first time I read, submit, review or run a journal.

parts.name: Role guides
parts.what: Short first-run screens and helpful empty pages for readers, authors, reviewers and editors, on the kit's first-run guide.

features.name: Help and support
features.does: Find plain help on submitting, rights, reviewing and citing, and reach support from any screen.

parts.name: Research help articles
parts.what: Short how-to pages for every feature, translated, in the kit's help centre, with glossary entries for terms such as preprint, accepted manuscript and DOI.

parts.name: Support for authors and editors
parts.what: Support cases linked to a submission or a journal, on the kit's support cases.

features.name: Institution accounts
features.does: Let a library or department set up an organisation, see its researchers' papers and help cover running costs.

parts.name: Institutions on the kit's organisation model
parts.what: Adds institution types (university, institute, library, department, funder) with their ROR ID to the kit's organisations.

parts.name: Institution sign-in
parts.what: Lets researchers sign in through their institution's own identity provider, through the kit's organisation sign-in.

features.name: Let a helper prepare my submissions
features.does: Let a co-author or research assistant fill in a submission for me, while I approve and post it myself.

parts.name: Submission helpers
parts.what: Scoped access for a helper to fill in a submission; the author still makes the rights declaration and posts.

areas.name: Search, browse and following
areas.summary: Finding research: full-text search with plain filters, browsing by field, following people, fields and journals, feeds for other tools, and separate human and AI sections.

features.name: Search papers
features.does: Search titles, abstracts, full text, authors and references, and filter by field, date, status, licence and language.

parts.name: Research search index
parts.what: Declares papers, versions, reviews, authors and journals to the kit's search service, with full text from the reading view and fields for status, licence, data and code.

parts.name: Search screen and filters
parts.what: A search box with filters for field, date, reviewed or not, has data, has code, licence and language, and results that show each paper's status in words, on the kit's search screens.

parts.name: Published ranking rules
parts.what: Results ranked by match and date under rules anyone can read, with no paid placement and no boost for any journal or institution.

parts.name: Search by ID
parts.what: Finds a paper straight from a pasted DOI, permanent link, preprint server ID or ORCID iD, and supports author: and title: terms.

features.name: Browse by field
features.does: Browse new and reviewed papers in a field, a subfield or a journal.

parts.name: Field list
parts.what: An open list of research fields and subfields under a licence that allows reuse, mapped to the fields open catalogues use, so papers line up across services.

parts.name: Field pages
parts.what: New this week, recently reviewed, journals in the field and recent updates, for each field.

features.name: Follow people, fields and journals
features.does: Follow people, fields and journals and get their new papers by email, in the app or in a feed.

parts.name: Follows and alerts
parts.what: Follows kept for each person, with new papers sent through the kit's notification router as single alerts or daily and weekly digests.

features.name: Save a search
features.does: Save a search and be told when new papers match it.

parts.name: Saved research searches
parts.what: Uses the kit's saved searches with the research filters and the person's chosen channels.

features.name: Feeds for other tools
features.does: Get any field, journal, author or search as a feed, and let other archives harvest our records.

parts.name: Atom and RSS feeds
parts.what: A feed for every field, journal, author and saved search, with no tracking.

parts.name: OAI-PMH endpoint
parts.what: Serves all metadata over OAI-PMH, the open protocol archives and catalogues use to harvest each other, in Dublin Core and JATS.

features.name: Human and AI sections
features.does: Choose to see papers written by people, papers generated by AI, or both.

parts.name: Human and AI sections
parts.what: Every paper declares its AI use; papers whose text or results were generated by an AI system go in the AI section, and each reader picks which sections they see.

parts.name: Wrong-section reports
parts.what: Anyone can flag a paper in the wrong section; moderators move it with the reason in the public log, and the authors can appeal.

features.name: Find related work
features.does: See what a paper cites, what cites it, and papers on similar topics with the reason shown.

parts.name: Citation links
parts.what: Shows each paper's references and cited-by list from open citation data and our own extracted references.

parts.name: Similar papers
parts.what: Suggests papers with similar text and references, says why, and runs only when the reader turns suggestions on.

features.name: Reading lists
features.does: Keep private or shared reading lists and export them to a reference manager.

parts.name: Reading lists
parts.what: Saved papers in named lists, private or shared by link, on the kit's favourites and sharing.

parts.name: List export
parts.what: Exports a list as BibTeX, RIS or CSL-JSON.

features.name: Search in my language
features.does: Search in my language and find papers whose titles and abstracts were written or translated into it.

parts.name: Search across languages
parts.what: Indexes every language a title and abstract is given in, with accent- and macron-aware matching.

features.name: Search other open archives
features.does: Search papers held elsewhere from the same box, each result linking to where it lives.

parts.name: Search beyond Spare Research
parts.what: Adds results from open catalogues whose terms allow it, labelled with their source, and links out to the paper where it lives.

areas.name: Reading a paper
areas.summary: The paper page and the reading experience: a clear landing page, a reflowing web view built from open XML, the PDF, figures, maths and references, readable on any screen and counted without tracking.

features.name: Paper page
features.does: Open one page with the title, authors, abstract, status, licence, versions, files, reviews and how to cite.

parts.name: Paper landing page
parts.what: A fast, server-rendered public page for every paper and version on the kit's public pages, showing its status (preprint, under review, reviewed, corrected, retracted) in words, not only colour.

parts.name: Machine-readable metadata
parts.what: Adds the citation meta tags scholar search engines read, schema.org ScholarlyArticle data and Signposting links to every paper page, so tools find the PDF, licence and authors.

parts.name: Share cards
parts.what: Preview cards with the title, authors and status when a paper link is shared, built without tracking.

features.name: Read in the browser
features.does: Read the full paper as a web page that reflows on a phone, with sections, figures, tables and references.

parts.name: Full text as JATS XML
parts.what: Keeps each version's full text as JATS XML, the open NISO standard most journals use, as the one source for the reading view, search and archive copies.

parts.name: Web reading view
parts.what: Renders JATS as a clean, reflowing page with a contents list, figure and table views, reference popups and links to each section.

parts.name: Maths in the reading view
parts.what: Shows equations as MathML with the TeX source copyable, using an openly licensed renderer whose licence suits the core.

parts.name: Linked references
parts.what: Each reference shows its DOI link, an open copy where one exists, and whether it was corrected or retracted.

features.name: Read and download the PDF
features.does: Read the PDF in the page or download it, with the paper's permanent link on it.

parts.name: PDF viewer
parts.what: Shows the PDF in the page through the shared PDF engine, with page thumbnails and search.

parts.name: Download with a stamp
parts.what: Adds a small line on each page with the permanent link, version and licence; the authors' original file stays available unchanged.

features.name: Accessible papers
features.does: Read papers with a screen reader, a keyboard, large text or high contrast.

parts.name: Accessible reading view
parts.what: The reading view built and tested to WCAG 2.2 AA on the kit's components, with MathML that screen readers can speak and figures that carry descriptions.

parts.name: Figure descriptions at submission
parts.what: Asks authors for a short description of each figure and flags missing ones, on the kit's image descriptions.

parts.name: Accessible PDF from the reading view
parts.what: Makes a tagged, accessible PDF from the JATS when the authors' PDF is not accessible.

features.name: Read on a phone or a slow connection
features.does: Read comfortably on an old phone or a slow link, with figures loading only when wanted.

parts.name: Light reading mode
parts.what: Text first, figures on tap and small pages, on the kit's light mode.

features.name: Reads and downloads without tracking
features.does: See how often a paper is read and downloaded, counted without tracking anyone.

parts.name: Private usage counts
parts.what: Views and downloads counted in totals only, with robots removed by a published rule, on the kit's private usage counts.

parts.name: Usage counting rules
parts.what: Whether to follow the COUNTER Code of Practice so counts compare with other publishers, and how to do it without personal data (*unverified* fit).

features.name: Plain-language summary
features.does: Read a short summary in plain words written by the authors.

parts.name: Plain-language summary
parts.what: An optional summary shown above the abstract, which can be translated.

features.name: Notes on a paper
features.does: Highlight and note a paper privately or share the notes with a group.

parts.name: Notes on papers
parts.what: Private and group notes anchored to text, kept on the W3C Web Annotation model so they can be exported.

features.name: Listen to a paper
features.does: Have a paper read aloud, skipping references and reading equations sensibly.

parts.name: Read aloud
parts.what: Reads the web view aloud with the kit's open voices.

features.name: Print and read offline
features.does: Print a clean copy or save papers to read offline.

parts.name: Offline papers
parts.what: Saves chosen papers on the device for reading offline, with a print layout.

features.name: Read a translation
features.does: Read a machine translation of a paper, clearly labelled, with the original one tap away.

parts.name: Paper translation
parts.what: Machine translation of the web view through the kit's translation service, never replacing the original.

areas.name: Submitting a paper
areas.summary: From files to a posted paper: upload in common formats, details and authors with ORCID and ROR, a licence, declarations and the rights check, by a person or through the same commands a script uses.

features.name: Start a submission
features.does: Start a submission, save it and come back later.

parts.name: Submission model
parts.what: A submission with its files, details, authors, licence, declarations and rights answers, every change an operation.

parts.name: Submission steps
parts.what: A short flow (files, details, licence, rights, declarations, check and post) that saves as it goes and works on a phone.

features.name: Upload the manuscript
features.does: Upload a PDF, a Word or OpenDocument file, or LaTeX source.

parts.name: Manuscript upload
parts.what: Resumable uploads with safety scanning and checksums, on the kit's file uploads.

parts.name: PDF checks
parts.what: Checks a PDF opens, has real text, embeds its fonts and is not locked, and says in plain words how to fix it.

parts.name: LaTeX build service
parts.what: Builds LaTeX source in a locked-down sandbox with no network, as a separate service, so TeX's many licences stay out of the core.

parts.name: Word and OpenDocument upload
parts.what: Reads .docx and .odt files through the shared office formats engine.

features.name: A web version made for me
features.does: Get a readable web version of my paper made automatically, and fix it before posting.

parts.name: Conversion method
parts.what: How to turn LaTeX, Word and PDF into JATS: which open converters exist, their licences and the quality each reaches. Pandoc is GPL, so it can only run as a separate tool or be learned from.

parts.name: Conversion to JATS
parts.what: Converts each upload to JATS with the chosen method, keeping figures, tables, maths and references.

parts.name: Check the web version
parts.what: Shows the author the web version beside the PDF before posting, lists any problems, and lets them fix headings, figures and references.

features.name: Details and authors
features.does: Enter the title, abstract, field, keywords and funding, and list every author with their part in the work.

parts.name: Paper metadata
parts.what: Title, abstract, keywords, field, language, funders and grant numbers, and dates, in one model that maps to Crossref, DataCite, JATS and Dublin Core.

parts.name: Author list
parts.what: Authors in order with ORCID iDs, ROR affiliations, the corresponding author and each person's contribution from the CRediT roles (an ANSI/NISO standard).

parts.name: Co-author confirmation
parts.what: Tells every co-author and asks them to confirm they agree to posting; the paper waits until all confirm or a set time passes with no objection.

parts.name: Details read from the file
parts.what: Fills in the title, authors, abstract and references from the upload for the author to check.

features.name: Choose a licence
features.does: Pick how others may reuse my paper, with each choice explained in plain words.

parts.name: Licence records
parts.what: The chosen licence kept as a machine-readable link in every metadata record and on every file.

parts.name: Licence chooser
parts.what: Creative Commons licences explained plainly, with CC BY 4.0 suggested because many funders ask for it, and any funder's requirement shown.

features.name: Declarations
features.does: Declare funding, competing interests, ethics approval, data availability and AI use.

parts.name: Declaration forms
parts.what: Funding, competing interests, ethics approval, trial registration, and data and code availability, on the kit's form model and shown on the paper page.

parts.name: AI use statement
parts.what: Every paper states whether and how AI tools were used: none, help with language or code, or text or results generated by AI. This also sets its section.

features.name: Check and post
features.does: See everything in one place, fix anything missing, and post.

parts.name: Final check
parts.what: One page listing anything missing or failing, with links back to fix it.

parts.name: Post a paper
parts.what: Posts version 1: gives it a permanent ID, queues its DOI, sends it to screening, and tells the authors what happens next.

features.name: Who can publish
features.does: Know the rule for who can post a paper, and ask for an endorsement if I need one.

parts.name: Who-can-publish rule
parts.what: The rule members choose (any account, a linked ORCID iD, or endorsement by someone already publishing in the field), kept as a setting changed only by vote.

parts.name: Endorsements
parts.what: A new author asks someone who has published in the field to endorse them; the endorser sees the paper first and is named in the record.

features.name: Submit from a script or agent
features.does: Prepare a submission from a script or an AI agent, with a person making the declarations and posting.

parts.name: Submission commands
parts.what: Every submission step as a command in the kit's command API and MCP server; declarations and posting are people-only actions.

features.name: Send to a journal
features.does: Ask a journal run on Spare Research to review my posted paper.

parts.name: Send to a journal
parts.what: Sends a posted paper to a chosen journal, showing its scope, review model and typical times first.

features.name: Bring a paper from another archive
features.does: Bring in a paper I already posted elsewhere, linked to the original.

parts.name: Import terms
parts.what: What each preprint server's terms and licences let us copy, and when only a link is allowed.

parts.name: Import from other preprint servers
parts.what: Brings in an author's own paper by its ID through the other server's published API, once the author proves it is theirs, and links back to the original.

features.name: Notebook papers
features.does: Post a paper with live figures or notebooks readers can open.

parts.name: Notebook papers
parts.what: Accepts Jupyter notebooks and shows them as static pages, with running them at cost as a later step.

areas.name: Rights, licences and publisher agreements
areas.summary: Hosting only what authors have the right to share: plain guidance on each version, publisher policies looked up, each country's rules, a recorded declaration, embargoes, rights retention, and takedowns that leave a clear notice.

features.name: Know what I may share
features.does: See in plain words which version of my paper I may post, and on what conditions.

parts.name: Versions explained
parts.what: Explains the preprint, the accepted manuscript and the published version, and that usually only the first two are the author's to share.

parts.name: Policy data terms
parts.what: Jisc's Open Policy Finder (formerly Sherpa Romeo) needs an API key and licenses its data under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: get Jisc's written confirmation that a non-profit may show it, and decide what to do when a journal is missing.

parts.name: Publisher policy lookup
parts.what: Looks up the journal a paper went to in Open Policy Finder where its terms allow, and shows the version, embargo, licence and conditions it lists.

features.name: Rights check before posting
features.does: Answer a few questions so the app can tell me whether I can post, and what I must add.

parts.name: Rights questions
parts.what: Who wrote it, was it accepted or published, which version is this, was an agreement signed, is any figure someone else's; the answers lead to post now, post on a date, or do not post.

parts.name: Rights declaration wording
parts.what: Plain wording for what authors confirm and what the co-op relies on, checked by a lawyer.

parts.name: Rights declaration
parts.what: The submitting author confirms they have the right to share this version under the chosen licence; the statement and its wording version are kept with the paper. A person must make it, never an agent.

features.name: Country rules for rights
features.does: See what my country's law adds, such as a right to share publicly funded work after a set time.

parts.name: Secondary publication rights research
parts.what: Which countries give authors a legal right to share their work after a period, which contracts cannot override, and the conditions in each: Germany and Austria (accepted manuscript after 12 months), France and Belgium (6 months, 12 in the humanities), the Netherlands (a reasonable period), and countries with none found, such as New Zealand (*to confirm*).

parts.name: Rights rules packs
parts.what: Each country's rights rules as data in its country pack, so the rights check can say what the law allows there.

features.name: Funder and institution policies
features.does: See what my funder or institution asks, such as immediate open access or a set licence.

parts.name: Funder policy data
parts.what: Open access rules of funders and institutions as data, each with its source and date, starting with policies published openly.

parts.name: Rights retention helper
parts.what: Adds a rights retention statement to a manuscript before it goes to an outside journal, so the author keeps the right to post the accepted version, as some funders ask.

features.name: Embargoes
features.does: Post now and have a version go public on a set date.

parts.name: Embargo timer
parts.what: Holds a version private until a date and then publishes it on the kit's durable timers, with the date shown on the page.

features.name: No paywalled copies
features.does: Trust that the archive holds only papers their authors may share.

parts.name: Publisher-version check
parts.what: Flags uploads that look like a publisher's typeset version (layout, running heads, publisher marks) for a screener to check against the rights answers.

parts.name: Already-published check
parts.what: Matches the title and authors against open DOI metadata and warns when a published version exists, linking to it.

features.name: Keep my copyright
features.does: Read a short agreement that leaves my copyright with me.

parts.name: Author agreement
parts.what: A short non-exclusive licence: authors keep their copyright, and the co-op may host, convert formats and copy to preservation archives.

features.name: Licence shown everywhere
features.does: See how I may reuse a paper on its page, in its files and in its metadata.

parts.name: Reuse guide
parts.what: Shows the licence with what it allows in plain words and how to credit the authors.

features.name: Copyright complaints and takedowns
features.does: Have a rights complaint about a paper handled fairly, with a notice left in its place.

parts.name: Copyright notice flow
parts.what: Notices and counter-notices about papers on the kit's copyright notice handling, with the authors told and heard.

parts.name: Tombstone pages
parts.what: When files must come down, the page and its permanent link stay with the metadata and a plain reason, so citations never break.

features.name: Material reused from others
features.does: Record permission for figures or text reused from others.

parts.name: Reused material log
parts.what: Lists reused figures with their source and permission or licence, shown in the caption.

areas.name: Screening before posting
areas.summary: Quick checks by trained members before a paper goes live: in scope, complete, not copied, safe, lawful and careful with people in the data. Screening is not peer review, and every decision has a reason.

features.name: Screening queue
features.does: Have my paper checked by a trained member within a published time.

parts.name: Screening queue
parts.what: Papers wait in the kit's review queue for screening, with published target times and a reason for every hold or decline.

parts.name: Screening rules
parts.what: A published, member-voted checklist: research, not advertising; in a listed field; complete, with authors and an abstract; readable; lawful.

parts.name: Screeners and their training
parts.what: Member screeners for each field, trained and certified on the kit's training module, with conflicts checked.

features.name: Copied text check
features.does: Know my paper was checked for copied text.

parts.name: Overlap check method
parts.what: Compares open methods for finding copied text with paid services, such as Crossref's Similarity Check, which costs extra on top of membership, on accuracy, cost and what text each can compare against.

parts.name: Overlap check
parts.what: Checks new papers against our own archive and openly licensed full text, showing matches to the screener as hints, never automatic verdicts.

features.name: Safety and ethics checks
features.does: Know papers that could put people at risk are held for a closer look.

parts.name: Ethics and trial checks
parts.what: Checks that studies on people or animals state ethics approval, and that clinical trials give a registry number, before posting.

parts.name: Personal details check
parts.what: Flags papers and files that may identify patients or participants, such as names, faces or exact dates, for the screener.

parts.name: Dangerous research rules
parts.what: What to do with papers that could help cause serious harm, such as weapons or dangerous pathogen work: who reviews them and which laws apply (*needs a lawyer*).

features.name: Health research posted with care
features.does: See a clear notice that unreviewed health research is not yet checked by experts.

parts.name: Health preprint notice
parts.what: A plain notice on unreviewed health research saying it should not guide treatment, as health preprint servers do.

features.name: Holds and appeals
features.does: Know why my paper was held or declined and ask for another look.

parts.name: Screening appeals
parts.what: The author gets the reason and can appeal to different members through the kit's appeals.

features.name: No junk in the archive
features.does: Not see adverts, junk or nonsense papers in the archive.

parts.name: Junk submission limits
parts.what: Limits on new accounts' submissions and signals for generated nonsense, on the kit's spam limits and fraud signals.

features.name: Screening figures in public
features.does: See how many papers were screened, held and declined, and how fast.

parts.name: Screening figures
parts.what: Counts and times through the kit's public reporting pipeline.

areas.name: Open peer review
areas.summary: Review in the open: authors or journals ask for review, conflicts are checked, reviewers comment on the paper itself, and reviews, author replies and assessments are published with their own DOIs. Whether reviewers are named is an open decision.

features.name: Ask for review
features.does: Ask for my posted paper to be reviewed, by a journal or by the community.

parts.name: Review requests
parts.what: A request for review linked to one version, from the authors or from a journal's editor.

features.name: Find and invite reviewers
features.does: Invite people with the right knowledge and no conflict with the authors.

parts.name: Reviewer pool
parts.what: People who offer to review, with their fields, languages and how many reviews they will take.

parts.name: Conflict of interest checks
parts.what: Flags recent co-authorship, a shared institution and declared conflicts, from ORCID and our own records, and asks each reviewer to confirm.

parts.name: Reviewer suggestions
parts.what: Suggests reviewers from fields and past papers, explains each suggestion, and leaves out anyone with a conflict.

parts.name: Invitations and replies
parts.what: Invites with the abstract and due date, accept or decline in one step, and reminders.

features.name: Write a review
features.does: Write a clear review, with comments on the exact lines they refer to.

parts.name: Review form
parts.what: Summary, strengths, concerns, questions for the authors, and an assessment of how well the evidence supports the claims, set by each journal or the default.

parts.name: Comments on the paper
parts.what: Comments pinned to text, figures and equations in the web view, on the kit's anchored comments.

parts.name: Reviewer guide
parts.what: Short guidance on fair, specific and kind reviews, and what not to do.

features.name: Named or anonymous reviews
features.does: Know whether my name will be shown, and choose where the journal allows.

parts.name: Review identity modes
parts.what: Named; anonymous to the public but known to the editor; or kept private: as each journal or the members decide, shown on every review.

parts.name: Anonymity protection
parts.what: Strips names and hidden data from review files and keeps anonymous reviewers out of public metadata and exports.

features.name: Published reviews
features.does: Read the reviews, the authors' reply and the editor's assessment next to the paper.

parts.name: Publish reviews
parts.what: Reviews, author replies and assessments published with the version they refer to once the round closes.

parts.name: Review DOIs
parts.what: Registers each published review as peer review content with the DOI agency, linked to the paper, so reviews can be cited.

features.name: Reply and revise
features.does: Answer each review point and post a revised version.

parts.name: Author reply
parts.what: A reply linked to each review point, published with the reviews.

features.name: Credit for reviewing
features.does: Get credit for reviewing on my profile and my ORCID record.

parts.name: Review records
parts.what: Reviews listed on the reviewer's profile, signed or counted only, and added to their ORCID record with consent.

features.name: Due dates and reminders
features.does: Know when a review is due and be reminded.

parts.name: Review due dates
parts.what: Due dates, reminders and gentle chasers on the kit's durable timers, with extensions on request.

features.name: Reviews by people
features.does: Trust that reviews are written by people, with any AI help declared.

parts.name: People-only reviews
parts.what: Sending a review is a people-only action; reviewers declare any AI help and agree never to paste unpublished papers into outside AI tools.

features.name: Respectful reviews
features.does: Know reviews are checked for personal attacks before they are published.

parts.name: Review conduct check
parts.what: The editor sees each review before it is published and can send back one that attacks people, under published conduct rules.

features.name: Reviews from other services
features.does: See reviews of the paper from other open review services.

parts.name: Review links with other services
parts.what: Sends and receives COAR Notify messages, so reviews from other open review services show on the paper and ours show there.

features.name: Comments from readers
features.does: Comment on a paper and read others' comments, with moderation.

parts.name: Comments on papers
parts.what: Signed comments on the kit's threads, with reports and member moderation.

features.name: Reviewer workload
features.does: Set how many reviews I take on, and let editors see who is overloaded.

parts.name: Review load limits
parts.what: Each reviewer sets a limit, invites stop when it is reached, and editors see the load across their journal.

features.name: Learn to review
features.does: Learn to review with a short course and examples.

parts.name: Reviewer course
parts.what: A short course with sample papers and published reviews, on the kit's training module.

areas.name: Journals on top and editorial work
areas.summary: Editors run journals as lists of papers they reviewed and accepted, on top of papers already posted: set-up, scope and policies, an editorial queue, decisions and assessments, issues where wanted, and protected journal names.

features.name: Start a journal
features.does: Set up a journal with its name, scope, editors, review model and policies.

parts.name: Journal model
parts.what: A journal with its scope, fields, editors, review model, review identity mode, policies and accepted papers, as an organisation on the kit's model.

parts.name: Journal set-up
parts.what: A guided set-up with plain choices and the policies a journal must publish.

parts.name: Protected journal names
parts.what: Checks new journal names against existing journals' titles and ISSNs, and holds lookalikes for a person to review, so nobody passes off a journal as another.

features.name: Editors and roles
features.does: Invite editors and give each a role, with conflicts declared.

parts.name: Editorial roles
parts.what: Editor-in-chief, handling editor, managing editor and screener roles on the kit's roles and team management, each with conflict declarations.

features.name: Editorial queue
features.does: See every paper sent to the journal, its stage and what it waits on.

parts.name: Editorial queue
parts.what: Papers by stage with due dates, reviewer status and the next step, filtered by editor.

parts.name: Assign a handling editor
parts.what: Gives a paper to an editor after checking conflicts.

features.name: Decisions and assessments
features.does: Make a decision or write an assessment, and tell the authors.

parts.name: Decision types
parts.what: Accept into the journal, ask for changes, or decline; or, for journals that do not accept or reject, a published assessment of how important the work is and how strong its evidence.

parts.name: Decision letters
parts.what: Templates for decision letters that link to the reviews, sent through the kit's messages.

features.name: Journal pages
features.does: Read a journal's scope, editors, policies and accepted papers on one page.

parts.name: Journal home page
parts.what: Scope, editors, review model, policies and papers, with feeds, on the kit's public pages.

parts.name: Policy pages
parts.what: Peer review, ethics, corrections, conflicts, licence and preservation policies written once from templates and shown on the journal page, as directories of open journals ask.

features.name: A journal's own web address
features.does: Run a journal under its own web address.

parts.name: Journal domains
parts.what: Connects a journal's own domain on the kit's custom domains.

features.name: Issues and volumes
features.does: Group accepted papers into volumes and issues where the field expects them.

parts.name: Issues and volumes
parts.what: Optional volumes, issues and article numbers, kept in the metadata.

features.name: An ISSN for the journal
features.does: Get an ISSN, with my country's steps shown.

parts.name: ISSN steps
parts.what: How to apply to each country's national ISSN centre, kept in its country pack, and where the number is recorded.

features.name: Themed collections
features.does: Gather papers on a theme with guest editors.

parts.name: Collections
parts.what: Themed collections with guest editors and their own page.

features.name: Move a journal in
features.does: Bring an existing journal with its papers, DOIs and history.

parts.name: Import from other journal systems
parts.what: Imports papers, public reviews and metadata from other open journal systems through their published export formats and OAI-PMH.

parts.name: DOI transfer
parts.what: Points a journal's existing DOIs at Spare Research through the DOI agency's own transfer process.

features.name: Journal figures
features.does: See open figures such as time to decision and reviews per paper, never one ranking number.

parts.name: Journal figures
parts.what: Time to first review and to decision, reviews per paper and corrections, through the public reporting pipeline.

areas.name: Versions, corrections and retractions
areas.summary: The record stays honest: every version kept and compared, corrections and expressions of concern linked to what they correct, retractions that leave the paper readable with a clear notice, and one public log of every change.

features.name: Post a new version
features.does: Post a new version with a short note on what changed.

parts.name: Version model
parts.what: Versions v1, v2 and on, each with its own files, date and note, kept for good; the permanent link leads to the latest and each version has its own link.

parts.name: New version flow
parts.what: The submission flow for a new version, carrying the details over and asking what changed.

features.name: See and compare versions
features.does: See every version and what changed between them.

parts.name: Version list
parts.what: Every version with its date and note on the paper page, and a clear notice when reading an older one.

parts.name: Compare versions
parts.what: Shows the text changes between two versions from their JATS.

features.name: Corrections
features.does: Read a correction linked to the paper it corrects.

parts.name: Correction notices
parts.what: A correction with its own page and DOI, linked both ways to the version it corrects, issued by the authors or editors with a reason.

parts.name: Update metadata
parts.what: Sends corrections, retractions and new versions to the DOI agency as updates, so other services show them too.

features.name: Expressions of concern
features.does: See when editors have a concern under investigation.

parts.name: Expression of concern
parts.what: A notice that an investigation is open, shown on the paper and in its metadata, and closed by a later notice.

features.name: Retractions
features.does: Know a retracted paper at once, with the reason and who decided.

parts.name: Retraction process
parts.what: A published process following COPE's retraction guidelines (updated in 2025) and NISO's recommended practice for retractions: who can decide, how the authors are heard, and what the notice must explain.

parts.name: Retraction notices
parts.what: A notice with the reason, who decided and when; the paper stays readable with a clear banner and a mark on every PDF page.

parts.name: Honest error label
parts.what: Says plainly when authors retracted their own paper over an honest error, so correcting the record is not treated as misconduct.

features.name: Withdraw a preprint
features.does: Withdraw my preprint, leaving a notice and the earlier versions on record.

parts.name: Withdrawal
parts.what: Authors withdraw a preprint with a reason; a withdrawal notice becomes the latest version and earlier versions stay, as preprint servers do.

features.name: Removal for legal reasons
features.does: Know when content was removed for a legal reason, and why.

parts.name: Legal removals
parts.what: Files removed only for a legal reason or a serious risk to people, leaving a tombstone, the rule and an entry in the public log.

features.name: One log of every change
features.does: Browse every correction, concern, retraction and withdrawal across the archive.

parts.name: Public updates log
parts.what: Every notice by date, field and journal with its reason, through the kit's public reporting pipeline.

features.name: Updates reach readers
features.does: Be told when a paper I saved, cited or followed is corrected or retracted.

parts.name: Update alerts
parts.what: Alerts to people who saved or followed a paper, and a status check on every reference in new submissions.

features.name: Retractions elsewhere
features.does: See when a paper I cite was retracted by another publisher.

parts.name: Outside retraction data
parts.what: Uses the Retraction Watch data, which Crossref makes openly available under CC0, to flag retracted references.

areas.name: Citing, DOIs and permanent links
areas.summary: Every paper, version, review and dataset gets a link that never breaks: our own permanent IDs, DOIs from a registration agency, ORCID and ROR in the metadata, references linked and shared openly, and citations in any style.

features.name: Permanent links
features.does: Cite a link that will always lead to the paper.

parts.name: Permanent IDs
parts.what: Our own short, permanent ID for every paper, version and review, built on the kit's permanent IDs and never reused or changed.

parts.name: Link resolver
parts.what: Resolves permanent links after pages or servers move, and keeps working from a simple static copy if the app is down.

features.name: DOIs
features.does: Get a DOI for my paper so it can be cited and found anywhere.

parts.name: DOI agency choice
parts.what: Crossref (yearly membership from USD 200, plus a fee for each DOI such as USD 0.25 for a preprint and USD 1 for a journal article in 2026) or DataCite (EUR 2,000 a year plus an infrastructure fee, with no fee for each DOI), or both, and what fits papers, reviews and data.

parts.name: Which things get DOIs
parts.what: Whether each version gets its own DOI or one DOI leads to the latest, following how preprint servers and data archives do it.

parts.name: DOI deposits
parts.what: Builds and sends metadata deposits for papers, versions, reviews and updates, retries failures and checks every DOI resolves.

features.name: How to cite
features.does: Copy a citation in my style and export it to my reference manager.

parts.name: Citation export
parts.what: BibTeX, RIS and CSL-JSON for any paper, list or search.

parts.name: Citation styles
parts.what: Formats citations in common styles from the open Citation Style Language styles (CC BY-SA 3.0, credited as they ask), with a processor whose licence suits the core, such as hayagriva (MIT or Apache-2.0).

parts.name: Cite box
parts.what: A cite box on every paper with the permanent link, the DOI, the version and a copy button.

features.name: Author and organisation IDs
features.does: See ORCID iDs and ROR IDs in every citation record.

parts.name: IDs in metadata
parts.what: ORCID iDs, ROR IDs, funder IDs and grant numbers carried in every deposit and export.

features.name: References linked and shared
features.does: See each reference linked, and have my references shared openly.

parts.name: Reference extraction
parts.what: Pulls references and structure from uploads with an openly licensed extractor, such as GROBID (Apache-2.0), run as a separate service.

parts.name: Reference matching
parts.what: Matches references to DOIs through open metadata APIs and lets authors fix mismatches.

parts.name: Open references
parts.what: Deposits every paper's references openly with its DOI metadata, so citation data stays free.

features.name: Open metadata
features.does: Reuse all our metadata freely.

parts.name: Metadata under CC0
parts.what: All metadata (titles, authors, abstracts, references) published under CC0, apart from each paper's own licence.

parts.name: Open metadata sources
parts.what: Which open sources we read and on what terms: DOI agency metadata, ORCID, ROR (CC0), OpenAlex (CC0 data, an API with a free daily allowance and charges for heavy use), OpenCitations and the Retraction Watch data (CC0).

features.name: Cite data and code
features.does: Cite the exact dataset and code version behind a paper.

parts.name: Data and code citations
parts.what: Dataset DOIs and code archive IDs (SWHIDs) shown in the cite box and in the paper's metadata as related items.

features.name: Who cited a paper
features.does: See who cited a paper, from open data.

parts.name: Cited-by from open data
parts.what: Cited-by lists from open citation data and our own references.

features.name: Backup identifiers
features.does: Know links still work if a DOI agency fails.

parts.name: Backup identifiers
parts.what: Whether to also make free ARK identifiers as a backup to DOIs, and how to keep both pointing at the same place.

areas.name: Data, code and supplementary files
areas.summary: The evidence behind a paper: datasets with their own DOIs, code archived for good, previews of common files, care with personal and Indigenous data, and links to the specialist archives researchers already use.

features.name: Attach data
features.does: Upload my data with the paper or link to where it already lives.

parts.name: Data uploads
parts.what: Data files with checksums and a free allowance per paper, larger sets at cost, on the kit's file uploads and storage.

parts.name: Dataset DOIs
parts.what: A DOI for each dataset with its own metadata and licence, through the chosen agency.

parts.name: Links to data elsewhere
parts.what: Links to datasets in other archives by DOI, checked to resolve.

parts.name: Data availability statement
parts.what: A required statement saying where the data are, or why they cannot be shared.

features.name: Attach code
features.does: Link my code and have the exact version archived for good.

parts.name: Code links
parts.what: Links a public code repository at a tagged version, with its licence read from the repository.

parts.name: Code archiving
parts.what: Asks Software Heritage to archive the repository and records its permanent SWHID.

features.name: Preview files
features.does: Look at tables, images and notebooks in the browser before downloading.

parts.name: File previews
parts.what: Previews for CSV, spreadsheets, images, notebooks and plain text on the kit's preview service.

features.name: Supplementary files
features.does: Add supplementary files that stay with each version.

parts.name: Supplementary files
parts.what: Extra files tied to a version, each with a description, size and checksum.

features.name: Data about people
features.does: Share data about people only in ways that protect them.

parts.name: Data about people
parts.what: Rules for data from participants and patients: remove identifying details before sharing, record consent, and never post raw personal data, checked by a lawyer in each country.

parts.name: Controlled access
parts.what: Data described openly but released only to approved people under a signed agreement, decided by the authors or a data committee.

features.name: Indigenous data
features.does: Have Indigenous data cared for as its communities ask.

parts.name: Indigenous data principles
parts.what: Applies the CARE principles and each country's own principles, with the kit's Māori data principles in the New Zealand example, and shows Local Contexts labels on the data.

features.name: Describe data well
features.does: Describe data so others can find and reuse it.

parts.name: Dataset metadata
parts.what: Dataset details mapped to the DataCite schema: creators, dates, formats, sizes and methods.

features.name: Large datasets
features.does: Share large datasets without running out of space.

parts.name: Large data at cost
parts.what: Chunked uploads and storage at cost for very large sets, or a link to a specialist archive.

features.name: Open data and code badges
features.does: See whether data and code were checked by a reviewer.

parts.name: Open data and code badges
parts.what: Badges for open data, open code and results reproduced, given by reviewers under published criteria.

features.name: Run the code
features.does: Run a paper's code in the browser.

parts.name: Run code at cost
parts.what: Runs archived code in a sandboxed container, charged at cost.

areas.name: Author, reviewer and editor dashboards
areas.summary: One place for my work: my papers and their stage, what is waiting on me, reviews to write, messages with editors and plain counts, on a phone or a desk.

features.name: My papers
features.does: See every paper I wrote or submitted and its stage.

parts.name: My papers
parts.what: Drafts, in screening, posted, under review, revised, accepted, corrected; each with its next step.

features.name: What is waiting on me
features.does: See every task in one list: confirm authorship, answer reviews, fix a check.

parts.name: To-do list
parts.what: Tasks across papers, reviews and journals, with due dates.

features.name: A paper's progress
features.does: See each step a paper went through and what comes next.

parts.name: Paper timeline
parts.what: Every step with its date and who acted, drawn from the operation log.

features.name: Messages with editors
features.does: Talk to the editor or screener about my paper in one thread.

parts.name: Paper messages
parts.what: A message thread for each paper with its authors and editors, on the kit's chat service.

features.name: My reviews
features.does: See reviews I was asked for, am writing and have finished.

parts.name: My reviews
parts.what: Invites, drafts, due dates and published reviews.

features.name: Reads and citations of my papers
features.does: See reads, downloads and citations of my papers, with no tracking.

parts.name: My figures
parts.what: Reads, downloads and open citations for each paper and version.

features.name: Notifications
features.does: Choose which alerts I get and how.

parts.name: Research notifications
parts.what: Alerts for screening, reviews, decisions and updates on the kit's notification settings and inbox.

features.name: Editor dashboard
features.does: As an editor, see my journal's queue, late reviews and decisions to make.

parts.name: Editor dashboard
parts.what: The journal's queue, load and due dates at a glance.

areas.name: Research integrity and fraud
areas.summary: Keeping the record trustworthy: signals for paper mills, fake reviewers, image and citation tricks, all treated as hints for trained people, a way for anyone to raise a concern, and an integrity panel that decides in the open.

features.name: Raise a concern
features.does: Report a possible problem with any paper, even without an account.

parts.name: Integrity reports
parts.what: A report form on every paper and review, open to anyone, on the kit's reports, with the reporter's name kept from the authors on request.

features.name: Integrity panel
features.does: Know concerns are looked into by trained members, fairly and on time.

parts.name: Integrity panel
parts.what: Trained members drawn with conflict checks, following COPE's published guidance and hearing the authors before deciding.

parts.name: Published outcomes
parts.what: Each outcome becomes a correction, a concern, a retraction or no action, with reasons in the public log.

features.name: Paper mill signals
features.does: Know papers are checked for signs of mass-produced fake research.

parts.name: Paper mill methods
parts.what: How published, open methods spot paper mills (odd stock phrases, template text, reused images, sudden author changes) and which suit us.

parts.name: Paper mill signals
parts.what: Signals from the chosen methods shown to screeners and editors as hints with their evidence, never automatic verdicts.

features.name: Real reviewers
features.does: Trust that reviewers are who they say they are.

parts.name: Reviewer identity checks
parts.what: Reviewers link a proven ORCID iD and, for journal reviews, an institutional email or a record of past papers; reviewers suggested by authors are checked before they are invited.

features.name: Author list changes
features.does: Know late changes to the author list are checked.

parts.name: Author list changes
parts.what: Adding or removing authors after posting needs every author's agreement and a reason, shown in the history.

features.name: AI-generated text
features.does: Know AI use is declared, and that undeclared generated text can be flagged.

parts.name: AI text hints
parts.what: Signals for undeclared generated text shown as hints only, because detectors are often wrong, with the authors always heard.

features.name: Integrity figures
features.does: See how many concerns were raised and what happened.

parts.name: Integrity figures
parts.what: Counts and outcomes in the kit's transparency reports.

features.name: Image checks
features.does: Know figures are checked for duplication.

parts.name: Image duplication hints
parts.what: Finds reused or duplicated images within and across papers, starting from the kit's reused photo checks.

features.name: Citation tricks
features.does: Know citation rings and forced citations are watched for.

parts.name: Citation pattern hints
parts.what: Flags unusual self-citation and citation rings for editors to look at.

features.name: Share signals with other publishers
features.does: Know fraud found here can be shared with other publishers in a lawful way.

parts.name: Sharing integrity signals
parts.what: Which shared integrity services exist, who may join them, and what privacy law lets us share.

areas.name: Long-term preservation
areas.summary: Papers that outlive any server: open archive packages, copies held by outside preservation archives and national libraries, checked copies, bulk exports anyone can mirror, and a plan if Spare Research ever closes.

features.name: Copies kept outside
features.does: Know copies of every paper are held by archives outside the co-op.

parts.name: Preservation archive choice
parts.what: Compares outside preservation archives, such as CLOCKSS, Portico, LOCKSS networks and the Internet Archive, on cost, terms and what they take (*costs to confirm*).

parts.name: Archive packages
parts.what: Each version packed with its files, JATS, metadata and checksums in an open package format any archive can take.

parts.name: Archive deposits
parts.what: Sends packages to the chosen archives and records each receipt.

features.name: Legal deposit
features.does: Know papers are deposited with national libraries where the law asks.

parts.name: Legal deposit rules
parts.what: Each country's legal deposit duties for online publications, as data in its country pack. In the New Zealand example the National Library harvests online documents under a 2006 notice and publishers help when asked (*to confirm against the Act*).

parts.name: Deposits to national libraries
parts.what: Sends papers to national libraries in the way each asks.

features.name: Checked copies
features.does: Know stored files are checked and never silently damaged.

parts.name: Fixity checks
parts.what: Regular checksum checks on every file and backup, with repair from another copy.

features.name: Formats that last
features.does: Know papers are kept in formats that will still open in fifty years.

parts.name: Preservation formats
parts.what: Keeps the authors' files plus JATS and archival PDF, and records each file's format.

features.name: Whole-archive export
features.does: Download the whole archive, so anyone can keep a copy.

parts.name: Bulk exports
parts.what: Regular full exports of metadata (CC0) and openly licensed papers, with checksums, so others can mirror the archive.

features.name: If Spare Research closes
features.does: Know what happens to papers if the service ever ends.

parts.name: Closing plan
parts.what: Links keep working through archives and mirrors, DOIs are pointed at the archive copies, and the steward holds the data, on the kit's wind-down plan.

features.name: Mirrors
features.does: Run a mirror of the archive.

parts.name: Mirrors
parts.what: A read-only mirror package for member groups and libraries, on the kit's self-host package.

features.name: Format migration
features.does: Know old files move to newer formats when needed.

parts.name: Format watch
parts.what: Watches for formats at risk and converts copies, keeping the originals.

areas.name: Indexing and being found
areas.summary: Getting papers into the places researchers look: web and scholar search engines, open catalogues, directories of open journals, subject indexes and library systems, with metadata checked before it leaves.

features.name: Found in web search
features.does: Find our papers in web and scholar search engines.

parts.name: Scholar search readiness
parts.what: Pages, meta tags, site maps and PDF links laid out as scholar search engines' published inclusion guidelines ask.

parts.name: Site maps
parts.what: Site maps of every paper and version, updated as papers are posted.

features.name: In open catalogues
features.does: Find our papers in open research catalogues.

parts.name: Open catalogue feeds
parts.what: DOI deposits and OAI-PMH that open catalogues and repository aggregators harvest, with a check that papers appear.

features.name: Metadata checks
features.does: Know our metadata is complete before it goes out.

parts.name: Metadata checks
parts.what: Checks each deposit for an abstract, ORCID iDs, ROR IDs, references, licence and funders, and shows gaps to the authors.

features.name: Directories of open journals
features.does: Get a journal listed in directories of open journals.

parts.name: Directory application helper
parts.what: Checks a journal against the published criteria of open journal directories and gathers what the application needs.

features.name: Subject indexes
features.does: Get papers into the indexes my field uses.

parts.name: Subject index research
parts.what: What subject indexes in life sciences, physics, computing, economics and other fields ask for, such as full-text XML or a publishing record.

features.name: Library systems
features.does: Find our papers through my library's search and link tools.

parts.name: Library link support
parts.what: OpenURL support, title lists for libraries, and links that send readers to the open copy.

features.name: Commercial citation indexes
features.does: Know whether our journals can be listed in commercial citation indexes.

parts.name: Commercial index research
parts.what: What commercial citation indexes ask of journals and whether their terms fit us.

areas.name: Commands, AI agents and integrations
areas.summary: Everything a person can do, a script or AI agent can do through the same commands, with people-only actions kept for people; plus webhooks, fair bulk access, reference manager support and deposits to institutional repositories.

features.name: Use Spare Research from a script
features.does: Search, read, submit and review from a script through the same commands as the app.

parts.name: Research command schemas
parts.what: Every action described once as a command for the kit's command API, SDKs and command-line tool.

parts.name: Headless check
parts.what: The kit's release check that every action on every screen maps to a command.

features.name: Connect an AI agent
features.does: Let my AI agent search, read and draft for me, asking me before anything is posted or sent.

parts.name: Research tools for agents
parts.what: The MCP server for Spare Research, built from the command schemas, with paper text marked as outside content.

parts.name: What agents may not do
parts.what: Agents cannot be authors or reviewers, make declarations, post, vote or decide; other actions ask the person where it matters.

features.name: Reference managers
features.does: Save any paper straight into my reference manager.

parts.name: Reference manager support
parts.what: Meta tags, embedded citation data and export links that common reference managers already read, with nothing to install.

features.name: Webhooks
features.does: Be told when papers, reviews or updates are posted.

parts.name: Research webhooks
parts.what: Signed webhooks for new papers, versions, reviews and updates.

features.name: Fair bulk access
features.does: Download metadata and papers in bulk, fairly.

parts.name: Fair bulk access
parts.what: Published rate limits and bulk exports instead of scraping, with personal details limited by the kit's bulk copy limits.

features.name: Institutional repositories
features.does: Have my papers copied to my institution's repository automatically.

parts.name: Repository deposits
parts.what: Sends papers to institutional repositories through the SWORD protocol and COAR Notify, with the author's consent.

features.name: Add-ins
features.does: Add field-specific checks and review forms as add-ins.

parts.name: Research add-ins
parts.what: Sandboxed add-ins for checks, review forms and viewers on the kit's plugin host.

features.name: Writing tools
features.does: Send a paper straight from my writing tool.

parts.name: Writing tool links
parts.what: Submits from open writing tools through the command API.

areas.name: Accessibility, languages and countries
areas.summary: For researchers everywhere: every screen accessible, the interface and papers in any language and script, titles and abstracts in several languages, and a rules pack for each country's law and institutions.

features.name: Accessible screens
features.does: Use every screen with a screen reader or a keyboard.

parts.name: Accessible components
parts.what: Every screen on the kit's accessible components, tested with disabled researchers before release.

parts.name: Accessibility statement
parts.what: An accessibility statement and barrier reports for Spare Research.

features.name: Use it in my language
features.does: Use the app in my language, with local dates and numbers.

parts.name: Research interface translations
parts.what: All words on screen on the kit's translation framework, with research terms in the glossary for translators.

features.name: Papers in any language
features.does: Post a paper in any language, with its title and abstract in more than one.

parts.name: Titles and abstracts in several languages
parts.what: Authors give titles and abstracts in as many languages as they like, each marked with its language.

parts.name: Every script
parts.what: Right-to-left and non-Latin scripts in the web view and PDFs, on the kit's text engine.

features.name: Country rules packs
features.does: Use Spare Research with my country's law and institutions.

parts.name: Research rules in country packs
parts.what: Adds rights, legal deposit, ethics, ISSN centre and funder rules to each kit country pack, with New Zealand as the first worked example and others added as members ask.

features.name: Display settings
features.does: Change text size, contrast and motion.

parts.name: Display settings
parts.what: The kit's display settings applied to the web view and every screen.

features.name: Easy read
features.does: Read the submission and rights steps in easy-read form.

parts.name: Easy-read guides
parts.what: Easy-read versions of the submission and rights steps, on the kit's easy-read pages.

areas.name: Apps on every device
areas.summary: The shared Spareware frame in the research colour: in any browser, installable on phones and computers, with links that open the right screen and a command search.

features.name: Use it in any browser
features.does: Use Spare Research in any modern browser, on a phone or a desk.

parts.name: Research app shell

assess: Walk through a researcher's month (post a preprint, get it screened, be invited to review, review on a phone, reply to reviews, cite a paper, read a retraction notice): does every step land on a core feature, or is something missing?
Are the core features the smallest set for a first usable release? Should the first release be a preprint server with open reviews, and journals on top come next?

Peer review (open decision): reviews published with reviewers' names, published anonymously, or kept private as most journals do now. Should each journal choose, or members set one rule? Does the demo make each choice and its effect clear?

Who can publish (open decision): anyone with an account, researchers with an ORCID iD, or endorsement by someone already publishing, as arXiv does. What does each mean for junk, paper mills and new researchers with no network, and does the endorsement step in the demo feel fair?

DOIs (open decision): Crossref, DataCite or both; one DOI for each version or one for the paper; covered as a running cost or paid by each journal. What would the first year cost at 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 papers?

Rights: does the rights check in the demo keep paywalled copies out without blocking authors who may legally post? Who keeps each country's rules pack (secondary publication rights, funder policies) up to date?
Existing publisher agreements: what happens when an author signed their rights away, or the journal is missing from Open Policy Finder?
Screening: who screens, how fast, and with what checklist? Will readers ever mistake a screened preprint for a reviewed paper in the demo?
Review quality and fraud: are the reviewer identity checks, conflict checks and paper mill signals enough, and are signals always hints for a person rather than automatic verdicts?
Corrections and retractions: does the demo show updates openly and fairly, including the difference between an honest error and misconduct, and do updates reach other indexes?
Preservation: which outside archives and national libraries will hold copies, what do they cost, and do links keep working if Spare Research closes?
Indexing: what does it take for papers to show in scholar search engines, open catalogues, directories of open journals and subject indexes from the first release?
Health research: is the 'not yet reviewed' notice strong enough for unreviewed clinical work, and should health papers get extra screening?

Data about people and Indigenous data: are the rules for participants' data, controlled access and Indigenous data (CARE, and in the New Zealand example Māori data principles) right, and who are our partners in each country?

AI: does the demo make clear that every paper declares its AI use, AI-generated papers sit in their own section, agents can never be authors or reviewers, and unpublished papers never go into outside AI tools?

Legal: in each country, which parts need a lawyer before launch (the rights declaration, erasure beside a permanent record, defamation in published reviews, dangerous research, sanctions, legal deposit)?

Licences: can the tools we plan to use (reference extractor, citation processor and styles, maths renderer, LaTeX build, format converters) be used under our rules, with GPL and AGPL kept out of the core?
Does the demo use only our own names, look and icons, imitate no publisher's or preprint server's interface, and name other organisations only to say what we replace or work with?
Headless: can a script and an agent do everything in the demo through the same commands, with declarations, posting, reviews and votes kept for people?

Kit dependencies: Spare Research's first release needs the kit's search service, anchored comments, durable timers, public pages, review queue, preview service and PDF engine. Are they all core in the kit, and should anything here move down into the kit, such as the JATS store, reference extraction or citation styles?
Are the part sizes believable? Which large parts (conversion to JATS, the LaTeX build, DOI deposits, overlap checks, paper mill signals, the web reading view) should become work-board pieces first?
